title: Fluorescent cacao oil: A material suited for highlighting blood vessel in macro-scale dissection
author: Tomita, Toda, et al.

steps.title: Melt cacao oil and add dye
steps.instruction: Place a glass jar containing 50 g of solid cacao oil in a water bath at 60 °C until fully liquidized, then add 0.13 g of oil‑based UV fluorescent dye TP3400 (≈0.26 % w/w, within the 0.2–0.3 % range) and mix thoroughly.

steps.title: Maintain liquid FCO
steps.instruction: Keep the fluorescent cacao oil (FCO) at a temperature above 40 °C (e.g., in a 40 °C water bath) to prevent solidification; optional oil‑based color ink may be added without affecting fluorescence.

steps.title: Warm specimen to body temperature
steps.instruction: Immediately after euthanasia, place the animal on a water‑filled bed set to 40 °C so that the whole specimen reaches ≈40 °C (do not exceed this temperature to avoid tissue damage).

steps.title: Expose heart and inject FCO
steps.instruction: Using surgical scissors, open the thoracic cavity to expose the heart, then inject 5 ml of liquid FCO into the ventricle lumen with a 5 ml syringe attached to an extension tube and a 27‑gauge needle; seal the puncture site with Aron Alpha Super Jelly (Konishi Co., Osaka, Japan) to prevent leakage.

steps.title: Solidify FCO by cooling
steps.instruction: Transfer the injected specimen to a water bath at 20 °C and allow it to cool for 1 h so the FCO solidifies; avoid rapid cooling such as immersion in iced water because the solidified oil becomes fragile.

steps.title: Fix specimen in formalin
steps.instruction: After cooling, fix the animal in 10 % formalin (or 5–10 % formalin) at room temperature (≈25 °C, reported as ≈30 °C in some sections) for adequate fixation.

steps.title: Dissect and observe vasculature
steps.instruction: Two weeks later, dissect the specimen using standard protocols, illuminate the exposed tissues with a UV penlight (WUBEN E19UV, Hiroshima, Japan) under dim ambient light, and capture images of the highlighted vascular network with an iPhone 11 and an Olympus Tough TG‑5 digital camera.
